text:
mike: Quick thread — proposal for a cost-aware soft-failover policy that respects tenant residency. Key idea: always prefer tenant's resident region; if that region is overloaded, try warm standby in a nearby region; only allow cross-region fallback for endpoints marked non-PII. Sharing draft policy below, looking for concerns (privacy, SLA, rollout complexity).

anna: This is attractive. Two questions: (1) how do we surface 'non-PII' marker to the routing layer? (2) what's client signal vs server heuristics?

li: my take: have opt-in per-tenant metadata + endpoint-level annotations. Default is conservative (no fallback). Also limit by cost multiplier and latency. If fallback used, mark request in audit log.

sara: operationally, we need inflight-KV-cache prewarm and a fast KV invalidation path. Otherwise a failover will see cache miss storms. recommend async prewarm + rate-limit fallback.

mike: agreed. think we should add an automatic cache prewarm: when host region's queue > 80% spin up standby and prefetch hot prefixes. Prewarm should be subject to cost guardrails.

li: also add a 'consent_required' flag for EU tenants — fallback disabled unless explicit consent. @legal can you confirm?

legal: Consent is OK if recorded. Default must be residency-enforced for sensitive data. We should require opt-in in contract language for cross-region serving of PII.

mike: here's a draft policy snippet:
```json
{
  "allow_fallback": "non_pii_only",
  "cost_multiplier": 1.3,
  "max_failover_latency_ms": 250,
  "prewarm": true
}
```

ops-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/geo-fallback (added to #runbooks)

anna: rollout plan: start with internal tenants, 1% traffic, observability hooks (trace tag, cost delta, quality sampling).

sara: add rollback signal: quality drop >= 2% or error rate spike > 0.5% => immediate rollback.

mike: ok i'll draft an RFC and canary playbook with test prompts + audit hooks. thanks all :thumbsup:
